audit.whatIsWrong: Page is labelled EVEN 5.5/10 on a 20% win rate, and rows 0, 3 and 6 of the chart disagree with the packet and with the mirror.
audit.why: Every why-string on the page describes Lillia losing lane — whys[3] ends 'so I'm surviving, not trading' while the row read Skill, and whys[0] describes being out-ranged completely while the row read Skill. The mirror already moved Level 1 and Levels 4-5 to Jayce and 2+ items to Lillia. A 20% win rate with five of seven stages conceded is a HARD matchup, not an even one.
audit.corrected: diff HARD at 8/10 with the red tone; chart set to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Jayce/Lillia in both layers with ratings moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second' Shock Blast window and nothing else on the page carries a number.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 16s at rank 1, and it shrinks to 6s at max, which is why the lane gets worse rather than better. Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1. The weapon swap itself is only 6s, so 'wait for hammer form' is not a real window. Lilting Lullaby is 150s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: 16s, 20s and 150s written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], both do's, the phases and the spike text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states the Dream Dust precondition on Lilting Lullaby, which the mirror identified as THE missing interaction in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot's text Drowsies only 'enemies with Dream Dust on them'. Against the longest-range lane bully in the role, a Lillia who has never landed a spell on Jayce cannot use her 150-second ultimate at all. The page describes it as a free delayed sleep in three places. The real rule — land Swirlseed or a Q FIRST — is also the thing that makes level 6 the one even stage.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[4], spikes[2], wants.you[1], mid and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings say his E knockback 'flips me into his hammer-form Q-E burst'.
audit.why: Thundering Blow (Hammer E) knocks the target AWAY, not toward him — Riot's text: 'Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back a short distance.' The gap is then re-closed by To the Skies! (Hammer Q), which leaps to an enemy and slows. Describing the knockback as a pull inverts the spacing the reader is supposed to manage.
audit.corrected: Thundering Blow named as a knock-back on 20s, To the Skies! as the re-closer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mercury Cannon's resistance shred is nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: on swapping to Cannon Stance, 'The first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist.' Against a squishy Lillia that is the opening beat of every burst he lands, and it explains why his poke hits harder than the raw numbers suggest.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[5], early, phases[5].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Acceleration Gate's effect on Shock Blast is only called 'gate-accelerated poke'.
audit.why: Riot's text is specific: fired through the gate, the missile's SPEED, RANGE and DAMAGE all increase. Missile speed is the part that matters — the dodge that works on a raw Shock Blast does not work on a gated one, and that is a concrete positioning rule.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[1], early, report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer — all seven whys plus early, mid and late — is written in first person ('me', 'I', 'my').
audit.why: The site is in second-person coaching voice. This is the worst case of it I have seen in this slice: ten strings.
audit.corrected: All ten rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: Jayce just out-ranges everything I have. His accelerated Q through the E gate and his cannon autos chip me from well outside my Blooming Blows sweetspot, so I can't even start the Dream Dust burn without eating two poke hits to land one. At level 1 I only have Q and concede the wave outright — last-hit from max range with the Q tip and accept I'm playing from behind. The thing to dodge above all is his E knockback: if he flips me, the hammer-form Q-E follow-up burst chunks my squishy body before my movement speed can carry me out.
edits.after: Jayce out-ranges everything you have. Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate gains speed, range and damage, and his cannon autos chip you from well outside Blooming Blows' 450, so you cannot start Dream Dust without eating two hits to land one. At level 1 concede the wave outright — last-hit from max range with the Q tip. Above all, respect Thundering Blow: it knocks you back on 20 seconds at rank 1, and Mercury Cannon's first attack cuts your armour and MR before the burst even begins.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are supposed to be my power window, but against Jayce it's just a survival window — my full Q and compounding burn don't matter if he's already poked me to half before I stack a single sweetspot. I farm with Q tip, weave my passive movement speed to dodge his ranged gate, and refuse to walk into cannon range to contest the wave. At 6 I finally get something: if I land E Swirlseed to slow and lay Dream Dust, Lilting Lullaby is a real anti-engage — the sleep punishes his cannon-form step-up and is the one moment this lane feels even. Bait his E knockback before I commit anything.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are supposed to be your power window; against Jayce it is only a survival window — full Q and the compounding burn don't matter if he poked you to half before you stacked one sweetspot. Farm with the Q tip, weave your move-speed stacks to dodge the gated Shock Blast, and refuse to contest inside cannon range. At 6 you get something: land Swirlseed to slow and lay Dream Dust FIRST, because Lilting Lullaby only Drowsies a target already carrying it — then that 150-second ult punishes his step-up. Bait Thundering Blow before committing.

edits.before: This is where I get back in it. Once Liandry's or Riftmaker lands, my W and Dream Dust DoT start doing serious percent-HP damage, and Jayce's poke lane lead stops mattering because I don't have to stand in front of him anymore. My passive and Q movement speed make me the best roamer on the map, so I convert into skirmishes and side-lane pressure where his single-target poke is far less scary than it was in a straight lane. I never re-enter a 1v1 poke war with him — I use the sleep to isolate a target in a teamfight and let my burn melt his squishy frame.
edits.after: This is where you get back in it. Once Liandry's or Riftmaker lands, your W and Dream Dust do serious percent-HP damage, and his poke lead stops mattering because you no longer have to stand in front of him. Blooming Blows' stacking move speed makes you the best roamer on the map, so convert into skirmishes and side-lane pressure where his single-target poke is far less frightening than in a straight lane. Never re-enter a 1v1 poke war — mark a target with Dream Dust, sleep it in a fight, and let the burn finish it.

notes: Worst voice problem in the slice: all seven whys plus early, mid and late were written in first person and are now second person. Two mechanical corrections: Thundering Blow knocks you AWAY (two strings said it flips you toward him), and Mercury Cannon's first attack in Cannon Stance reduces your armour and MR — absent from the page entirely despite being the opening beat of his burst. I also raised the headline from EVEN 5.5/10 to HARD 8/10: a 20% win rate with five of seven stages conceded cannot ship as even. Chart flips match the mirror's three rows and are one atomic group with their ratings.
